question: Does an all-layer on-policy route12/B20 run remain behaviorally and distributionally identical when every routed layer is composed as a B16 base plus the four-record B20 correction?

harness.runner_change: Allow the caller to select production defaults; these arms force 0 so the registered host-reference incremental path is used.

protocol.candidate: Same 20 records and means, but each routed expert output is accumulated as B16 followed by four exact-minus-mean corrections.
protocol.commands: Run exactly one control and one candidate per registered fixture with the clean committed source and one executable.
protocol.anti_tuning: Do not add fixtures, change budgets, change route count, alter expected IDs, or rerun an arm after observing output.

structural: Every candidate incremental marker reports base=16, full=20, delta=4.
Control and candidate account equal logical authoritative bytes and selected records.
All four arms use one executable hash, the registered model, clean source, host-reference execution and route12.
behavioral: Control and candidate generated ID sequences are byte-for-byte equal and match the frozen expected IDs.
Control and candidate final full-vocabulary logits are byte-identical for both fixtures.
The get_weather boundary remains native-correct at ID 163588.
distributional: KL(control B20 || incremental B20) is 0 for both fixtures.
Control and candidate terminal KL versus the aligned native teacher are equal for both fixtures.
gates.go: All gates pass. Earn a production-profile delta-only read/evaluate prototype and a separate risk predictor test; do not promote production.
gates.no_go: Any mismatch closes the current composition order.
gates.performance: No timing or throughput claim is permitted from host-reference arms.
